{{Notability|date=January 2026}}
A '''golden ellipse''' is an [[ellipse]] in which the [[aspect ratio]] of its two [[semi-axis|semi-axes]] <math>a</math> and <math>b</math> corresponds to the [[golden ratio]].

== Equivalent characterization ==
[[File:Goldene Ellipse.svg|thumb|upright=1.5]]
Given is a [[Annulus (mathematics)|annulus]] with outer [[radius]] <math>a</math> and inner radius <math>b</math> as well as an ellipse with semi-major axis <math>a</math> and semi-minor axis <math>b</math>, where <math>a</math> and <math>b</math> are positive [[real number]]s.

Then the ratio <math>\frac{a}{b}</math> corresponds to the golden ratio <math>\Phi</math> if and only if the annulus and the ellipse have the same area. <ref>A. D. Rawlins: in ''The Changing Shape of Geometry: Celebrating a Century of Geometry and Geometry Teaching'', Cambridge University Press (2003), ISBN 0-5215-3162-4, S. 308</ref>

The [[mathematical proof|proof]] results from the following equivalence chain:
<math display="block">\pi a^2-\pi b^2=\pi ab \Leftrightarrow a^2-ba-b^2=0 \Leftrightarrow a=\frac{b}{2}\ \pm\sqrt{\frac{b^2}{4}+b^2} \Leftrightarrow a=\frac{1}{2}(1 \pm \sqrt{5}) \cdot b</math>

Since only the positive solution is possible, after division by <math>b</math> we get:
<math display="block">\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{5})=\Phi</math>

== Relationship to the golden rectangle ==
[[File:Goldene Ellipse im Goldenen Rechteck.svg|thumb]]
The golden ellipse can be [[Inscribed figure|inscribed]] in a [[golden rectangle]] with the side lengths <math>2a</math> and <math>2b</math>.<ref name="Claudi Alsina">Claudi Alsina, Roger B. Nelsen: '' Perlen der Mathematik - 20 geometrische Figuren als Ausgangspunkte für mathematische Erkundungsreisen '', Springer Spektrum, Springer-Verlag GmbH Berlin 2015, ISBN 978-3-662-45460-2, page 141</ref>
